Das Prinzip ist simpel: Man muss in den 500 Leveln je die längste Linie malen. Der Herbst, die Jahreszeit in welcher man morgens durch gold gefärbten Nebel fährt und sich wünscht, man hätte einen Job mit Gleitzeit oder Homeoffice. Dann könnte man nämlich einfach am nächsten Waldstück anhalten und erstmal durch den mystischen Morgen stapfen. 
Ebenso Herbst, um einen herum ist im Prinzip ständig irgendwer krank. Und irgendwann ist man selbst dann auch wieder fällig. Also landet man wieder vor dem PC, wühlt sich durch den Steamshop und findet mit etwas Glück ein paar Spiele, die angenehm und ohne große Anstrengung von der Hand gehen. Lines ist ein solches Spiel.

Farben, Punkte, Formen. Aus den Punkten werden Linien, welche die Form füllen. Die Farbe, welche einem zugeordnet ist, soll am Ende den längsten Weg zurück legen. Also gilt es zu überlegen, wo man seinen Startpunkt hinsetzt, um die anderen Farben zu blockieren. In einem anderen Level kann man Linien durchtrennen - also muss man schauen, welche man nimmt, um den anderen Farben den Weg zu zerschneiden. Man kann auch Linien dazu setzen und damit seinen Weg verlängern - aber Achtung, ist die andere Farbe schneller am Ziel, so kann auch sie diese Strecke nutzen. Es gibt noch Level, wo man die Startpunkte der Konkurrenz einfach löschen kann - zumindest einen oder zwei - also überlegen, was sinnvoll ist. Portale gibt es auch. Man beamt sich in das "feindliche Lager" und durchkreuzt so die Wege und nimmt sie selbst ein. Das Ganze wird gekrönt mit einem Mix aus Allem. Hier kann man dann z.b. zunächst einen Punkt vom Gegner löschen, dann eine Zusatzstrecke bauen und eine Bahn durchschneiden (Reihenfolge und Möglichkeiten werden vom Spiel vorgegeben).  

Klingt vielleicht kompliziert? Ist es aber nicht. Es ist eigentlich recht einfach und logisch und macht Spaß. Man hat seine Wahl getroffen und die Farben breiten sich aus. Man sieht ihnen dabei zu und hofft, dass man nichts übersehen hat und die eigene (wird übrigens durch den Rahmen angezeigt) am weitesten kommt. Am Ende hat man eine bunte Form mit einer Übersicht (Prozente), wie sich die Farben anteilig verteilt haben. Das Level kann wiederholt werden oder man geht weiter. Man kommt in diesem Spiel auch voran, wenn man ein Level nicht schafft und kann später dann dorthin zurück kehren.

Die Errungenschaften sind ein Mix aus okay/sinnvoll und lästiger Beschäftigungstherapie. Letzteres kann man aber auch auslassen, dann fehlen halt ein paar.

Grafik/Aufmachung: angenehm, schlicht, übersichtlich. Man kann hell oder dunkel spielen und auch ein paar andere Dinge für sich einstellen. "Musik" ist auch passend, ich habe allerdings dann irgendwann meine eigene gehört. 

Zusätzlich bietet das Spiel einen Endlosmodus, tägliche Herausforderungen und einen Leveleditor. Diesen fand ich beim kurzen reinschauen recht kompliziert, aber das mag täuschen. Dazu kommen ein sehr geringer Preis und eine hohe Levelanzahl.

[b]My positives[/b]
[list]
[*] [b]There's a dark theme mode option, to switch from the default light theme mode[/b]; personally used this predominantly while playing!

[*] [b]The game has a built-in tracking system on each level, including custom levels, on having the amount of wins, losses, plays, and even the win streak; this also applies to the win percentage of 6 level packs.[/b]

[b]My negatives[/b]
[list]
[*] [b]Sometimes failing a level is due to a mix of luck and difficulty on finding a viable solution;[/b] personally, level 27 in Point mode, and level 51 in Rope mode were my biggest pain points for me.

[*] [b]There's no easy percentage of the ratio between wins and losses on each level the game keeps track of;[/b] the statistics are there, but no auto-converting percentage wise.

[*] [b]While using the level editor, the game crashes at random regardless of simplicity or complexity;[/b] even with saving of in-progress level work, when saving something while having a reference image, that upon reloading it, only the reference image isn't saved. Likely, I just start over because it's too tedious to realign the reference image to the set up lines.

[*] [b]There's no way to delete in-progress user level files during the game[/b]; can't find a way to delete them outside of the game as far as I know. While a minor nitpick, sometimes I wanna have a clean slate when I don't need to check those usermade levels I made anymore when I already uploaded them.

[*] [b]The level editor gets more laggy the more line nodes are added in a in-progress usermade level;[/b] one of the things I wanted to do is to make kinda complicated line art that would take time to think about and plan with the given tools in order to finish the levels deviated from the built-in levels, but sadly, the game starts to lag with more line nodes added, with mouse clicks and drags taking longer to respond.

[*] [b]Usermade levels take longer to load when wanting to play them compared to the built-in provided levels made by the developers;[/b] To test this, I recreated 30th level in the Mix mode, 'Traffic', the re-created usermade level still takes time to load, whereas playing the built-in level instead loads with no delay. My educated guess is that custom levels are handled differently from built-in levels when finding a valid solution, varying the amount of time. This is unfortunate when wanting to make or play usermade levels, that even levels similar to what the developers made, it still results in variable loading times. This most likely explains the relative low amount of usermade levels since game release, since as of this review, 72 usermade levels, of which I uploaded 12 of them.

[*] [b]Usermade levels are less likely to be played due to a lack of special mode for them compared to built-in levels which has the Infinite mode;[/b] I played Infinite mode to get the 'Marathon' Steam achievement without downloading a usermade level to speed up the process, and there has been a lack of usermade levels during the mode since I downloaded some of them through subscribing. Incase the usermade levels exclusion from Infinite mode is intentional, I feel there should some kind of special mode for the usermade levels. I don't think a Infinite mode for usermade levels would work if the point of Infinite mode is getting the highest win streak from a grab bag of 500 built-in levels, since people can just inflate their best scores for a hypothetical special mode by just playing easy levels.[/list]

[b]My eehs/neutral feelings[/b]
[list]
[*] [b]I have no opinion on the Twitch integration functionality, and whether it works or not, since I am not a Twitch streamer.[/b]

[*] [b]Certain colors for the dots will change when using either the default light theme mode or dark theme mode;[/b] in the default light theme mode, dots that are colored black remain black, while in dark theme mode, dots that are colored black are instead colored white. This is something you'll have to plan around when making new usermade levels.[/list]

Lines is a unique take on the puzzle genre on with the given tools for each level, to plan out a solution to ensure your color covers more than the enemy colors. I enjoyed it for the most part despite the various caveats in terms of usermade level creation and playing, which was one of the main reasons why I bought the game years ago on wanting to play and make more levels. I do wish there were updates regarding making usermade levels less of a hassle and more fulfilling, since that's one of the main differences between the Windows version and the iOS version is the level editor only in the Windows version. The iOS version and the Android version of the game still occasionally gets updates, which might imply the game developer, Gamious, is still around and existing.

I wish I can strongly recommend people to buy this game if both enjoying this gameplay concept and want to make usermade levels alongside me, but as it is, if you want to play this game free of advertisements in comparison to the mobile versions of the game, I recommend getting the game for the unique gameplay. I'll still come back to it mainly to make more levels to upload to Steam Workshop, even favoriting this game on Steam, a rarity for me to do. This review is based on version 1.2.1.0, which I assume was released on November 12, 2019.

The idea behind this game is interesting and somewhat fun, but not enjoyable enough to warrant the expected level of play.

Clearing the 500 levels will probably take ~5 hours tops, and then if you want to complete the achievements, you'll spend hours on end mindlessly replaying the levels to complete incredibly engaging achievements such as 'place 1000 points', 'cut 1000 lines', 'reach a distance of 10000 travelled' and so on... even though there's only ~100 levels per mechanic. I don't get why developers add mindless accumulation achievements like these.

I am 32 years old.

My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.

When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.

Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.

With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.

After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.

Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.

Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.

Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.

Thank you.

[h1]色彩涌动与平衡距离 - 单调，适合打发碎片时间[/h1]

[h1]前言与短评：[/h1]
大家好，是我十字字符哒。

这次跟大家分享的游戏叫Lines。

Lines是一款休闲益智类小品游戏，玩法简单，有五种不同模式，也有混合模式/每日挑战/无限模式可供挑战，共有500个关卡，(官方：)每个关卡还有200种变化。

看官方介绍及游戏画面确实令人期待，但实际上玩法还挺无趣，单一模式很乏，关卡就只是不同的图，同关卡所谓的200种变化有不少就只是位置稍有变化，甚至翻转下，变化不大。游玩感受就是单纯"通关"。

混合模式(每日/无限)虽组合多种模式，且有使用工具的固定顺序，比单一模式稍难，但也不能说的上有趣。

画面表现倒是挺好，线条与大块的图形构成UI，简洁又有设计感，而色彩涌动确实如steam游戏页表现的一样，流动的色彩很活跃，感受不错。SE是随色彩涌动、碰撞、相融，在选单跟操作时BGM跟SE结合的不错，而SE在结算(色彩涌动)时也算有趣，但玩久了就感觉SE很散(零碎)。

不能说差，只是玩法简单确实单调，或许更适合在手机上游玩。

[b]整体来说
《Lines》[/b]
一款休闲益智类小品游戏，透过点/切/连线/消除/传送来扩大自己颜色所占据的比例，看介绍及画面很令人期待，但实际游戏玩法稍显单调，单玩法很乏，不同关卡就只是不同的图，游玩感受就是单纯的"通关"。虽然混合模式组合多种玩法，且使用顺序固定，让游戏稍有挑战，但也不能说的上有趣。画面表现倒是挺好，简洁又有设计感，流动的色彩很活跃。整体来说，不适合长时间玩，或许更适合在手机上，利用碎片时间偶尔玩玩。

游戏性及内容表现：[/h1]

Казуальная игрушка-времяубивалка.

Нам даётся поле причудливой формы с расставленными точками — нашими и противников. В зависимости от режима игры, нужно добавить свои точки или убрать несколько точек противников, добавить свои линии на поле или разорвать линии уже имеющиеся. После этого из точек начинает литься краска, заполняя фигуру. Цель — закрасить больше всех.

Каждая мини-партия длится около полуминуты. Можно запускать как разные уровни, так один и тот же — каждый раз у точек разное местоположение, что, собственно, и заставляет немного подумать.
Это и плюс, и минус игры, потому что хотя это и даёт реиграбельность, иногда точки генерируются так, что выиграть просто невозможно.

Пожалуй, чему и может научить игра, так это оценивать расстояния между точками, чтобы прикинуть, как получше сыграть мини-партию.

Вряд ли имеет смысл играть длинными сессиями просто так; скорее эта игра подходит в виде фонового занятия.
Ну и сверх-простота игры делает её не слишком интересной для тех, кто хочет какого-нибудь вызова от головоломок.

A nice relaxing puzzle game. None of the puzzles are very difficult, and it didn't take long to get through the 250 puzzles that came with the game, as the vast majority of them were solved on the first or second go. 

The sound is particularly charming - quiet piano chords play as the lines progress and meet each other.

Great minimalist puzzle. The goal is easy : for each level, you're given a pattern made of lines, a color, and one or more enemies color dots. Your color must fill a longer line distance than your enemies. For this, you have 4 different tools :

[list]
[*]Point : add one or more of your color dots
[*]Eraser : remove one or more of your enemies dots
[*]Rope : add one or more lines to the pattern
[*]Knife : cut one or more lines from the pattern
[/list]

You use the tools given by the level, and the colors start to flow along the lines. Simple enough.

You have 50 levels dedicated to each of the above tools, plus 50 more levels with a mix of those tools (you don't get to choose which, it's predetermined). And you also have daily challenges (normal levels, which you must win 3 times in a row, 3 out of 4 times, for example, to win the challenge). And also user levels in the workshop (and a level editor, of course).

Graphics and sound effects do a very good job, and all of this makes an excellent and relaxing puzzle game.

There are a few flaws, though :

[list]
[*]Adding lines is sometimes tough to do. Same thing for cutting lines, when you need to do it at a very precise point.

[*]Starting positions are random (actually, I think there are a few predetermined positions, and you and the enemy are randomly placed on those fixed positions ... not 100% certain about this), which is good for replayability. However, I'm pretty sure (tough to demonstrate, though) you can end up with unwinnable starting positions (you can cancel a level if needed, except on daily challenges)

[*]And finally, there are some seriously stupid achievements :
[list]
[*]Win 5 daily challenges (fine), and win 25 daily challenges, which means that the game'll need to remain installed for at least a month, depending how successful you are at these challenges

[*]Win a level 3 times in a row, 5 times, 10 times (fine up to now, this is actually needed to unlock the last levels of each tool), 50 times (ouch) and 100 times (you gotta be kidding me). This is doable, but certainly not enjoyable. Let's say it takes 15 seconds to run a level, you'll have to play that same level 25 minutes in a row to get that last achievement (assuming you don't lose once in the process ...)

[*]For each tool, use it 250 times (mostly fine, it will be almost done after a normal playthrough), and 1000 times. Wth ? Depending on the tool, the most you will use on a level is either 3, 4 or 5. So at best, you'll have to play a level 200 times, at worst another one 333 times. Or if you replay the whole 50 levels of a tool (let's with an everage of 3 uses by level), you'll have to do everything something like 6 to 7 times. For each of the frigging tools. Ridiculous, and not enjoyable at all, I can tell you.

[*]And the last : cover a distance of 10000 (whatever the unit is) with your color. I did everything else (except the 25 daily challenges), including the 100 times in a row one, and 1000 uses of each tool, and I'm barely above a distance of 4000, i.e. not even halfway (after more than 13 hours).
[/list]
[/list]

At the time I'm writing this, the 25 daily challenges achievement has been done by 2.2% of owners, the 1000 uses of each tool by somewhere between 1.9 and 2.2% of users, and the 10000 distance one by 1.2% of people, that should speak by itself (and that's assuming they were unlocked in a legit way ;))

Anyway, unless you're looking for easy or enjoyable achievements, Lines is still a pretty good puzzle game at its core, so it's definitely recommended.

これに対して「どこに自分の点を置くか」「どの敵の点を消すか」「どこに追加の線を引くか」「どこの線を切断するか」という４つの行動が各ステージに既定数割り振られており、
いかに効果的に自分の色を伸ばし敵の色を削るか？といったパズルゲームとなっている。
